objects: SNP-based narrow-sense heritability h2; uneven LD
assumptions: SNP-based mixed-model heritability analysis with uneven LD
conclusion: Uneven LD can make SNP-based mixed-model heritability estimation highly sensitive despite robustness to other investigated assumptions.
scope: Motivating limitation stated from simulations; four other assumptions are unnamed in the abstract.
span: We investigated via simulation the validity of several key assumptions underpinning the mixed-model analysis used in SNP-based h2 estimation. Although we found that the method is reasonably robust to violations of four key assumptions, it can be highly sensitive to uneven linkage disequilibrium (LD) between SNPs: contributions to h2 are overestimated from causal variants in regions of high LD and are underestimated in regions of low LD.

conclusion: The described SNP-based approach estimates narrow-sense heritability from genome-wide SNPs genotyped in unrelated individuals.
scope: Abstract-level input description; phenotype requirements and likelihood are unspecified.
span: Estimation of narrow-sense heritability, h2, from genome-wide SNPs genotyped in unrelated individuals has recently attracted interest and offers several advantages over traditional pedigree-based methods.

conclusion: The target quantity is narrow-sense heritability estimated from genome-wide SNPs.
scope: SNP-based heritability target; abstract does not identify it with total pedigree heritability.
span: Estimation of narrow-sense heritability, h2, from genome-wide SNPs genotyped in unrelated individuals has recently attracted interest and offers several advantages over traditional pedigree-based methods.

span: The overall direction of the bias can be up or down depending on the genetic architecture of the trait, but it can be substantial in realistic scenarios.
